data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 relies on the Condorcet jury theorem's conditional independence assumption as its core mechanism, but this makes its evidence standard for distinguishing genuine gain from mere compliance circular and self-defeating. Its own overturn condition admits that high inter-panel correlation on errors the expert avoids would falsify independence. But the very checklist structure it analyzes imposes identical explicit criteria on identically trained non-experts, mechanically inducing correlated errors on any item where the checklist is incomplete relative to the outcome. The target never establishes how, within a single evaluation, one can separate a 'genuine reliability gain' from correlated checklist compliance that tracks right answers, because its aggregation mechanism presumes the independence that compliance恰恰 violates.
